To determine when Alice and Bob will meet for the second time at the starting point, we need to calculate the time it takes for each of them to complete one full lap around the track and then find the least common multiple (LCM) of these times. 

Alice's lap time is calculated as follows:
\[ \text{Lap time for Alice} = \frac{\text{Circumference}}{\text{Speed}} = \frac{1 \text{ mile}}{6 \text{ miles per hour}} = \frac{1}{6} \text{ hours} \]

Bob's lap time is calculated as follows:
\[ \text{Lap time for Bob} = \frac{\text{Circumference}}{\text{Speed}} = \frac{1 \text{ mile}}{4 \text{ miles per hour}} = \frac{1}{4} \text{ hours} \]

To find the time when they will meet for the second time at the starting point, we need to find the LCM of their lap times. First, convert these times to minutes:
\[ \text{Lap time for Alice in minutes} = \frac{1}{6} \times 60 = 10 \text{ minutes} \]
\[ \text{Lap time for Bob in minutes} = \frac{1}{4} \times 60 = 15 \text{ minutes} \]

The LCM of 10 and 15 is 30. Therefore, Alice and Bob will meet for the second time at the starting point after 30 minutes.
